The Senior Data Analyst II takes ownership of analysis and reporting from the first question to the final result. The work helps content move through our operations faster and more smoothly, supports better decisions based on facts, and speeds up ongoing improvement across our global teams. The role works with a high degree of independence: it turns loosely defined business questions into clear ideas to test, builds the right tools to answer them (dashboards, performance measures, and in-depth studies), and guides senior stakeholders with clear, story-driven insights. Karman is a fast-growing NVIDIA-backed AI company enabling AI data centers to dynamically orchestrate power and unlock more compute capacity from existing energy infrastructure. For over a decade, we have applied AI to the electric grid, bringing real-time visibility and power-flow control to complex energy infrastructure. Our Karman platform, built on a custom NVIDIA module, brings that same capability to AI data centers, giving operators a way to better use the power already available to them.

Your time will be split between improving the algorithms already in production and R&D for the next iterations of the product, from smarter forecasting and online learning to orchestration across larger portions of a data center and new generations of GPU hardware.

• Help to define how we measure algorithm performance, from adherence to electrical limits to impact on compute throughput, and build the benchmark and regression suites that hold each release to that bar

• Continuously improve the performance, robustness, and operability of the algorithm-driven services already in production

• Drive R&D that de-risks and shapes future product iterations (forecasting, automated parameter tuning, orchestration at larger scales, new compute and actuation hardware), running experiments in our lab and pilot environments and turning results into clear decisions

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics, mechanical or aerospace engineering, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience

• Deep expertise in control systems and mathematical optimization, including feedback control, state estimation, and the practical realities of latency, noise, and missing data, ideally in distributed or edge settings

description:
Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work - both in and out of the office.

About the role
Oura is rebuilding how it builds software. Every engineer has agentic tooling, and our own pipeline already takes a well-formed ticket to a reviewed, tested commit stack. It runs interactively, headless, and on a cloud sandbox fleet, with its own evals and tracing. We are looking for engineers who use AI as a fundamental building block of both the products we ship and the way we build them.
That is a strong start on one stage of the lifecycle. The next step is the whole loop. As a Staff Engineer on the AI Transformation team, you will architect and own the system that turns agentic development from something power users do into the way hundreds of engineers across iOS, Android, backend and AI services ship every day. That means spec and intake, planning, implementation, review, testing, CI/CD, release, observability and incident follow-up, each with agents doing real work and humans keeping judgment where it matters.
This is a fast-moving, LLM-forward team. We prioritize rapid prototyping, iterative loops and AI-native development, with the speed of a startup and the reach of a product used by millions of members. You can work remotely from anywhere in Europe, or hybrid from our offices in Helsinki, Oulu or Tampere.
You will build the pipeline, measure it, and make it trustworthy enough that teams choose it. Success is measured in validated changes reaching members faster and safer: time to a trustworthy signal, escaped defects, cost per merged change, and how many squads run on the paved path because it is better, not because they were told to.
What you will do
You don't need to do all of these on day one, but these are the kinds of problems you'll own:

•
Set the technical direction for the agentic pipeline: Make our existing ticket-to-PR pipeline dependable infrastructure. Own its architecture, including agent orchestration, context management and tool calling, and improve its reliability, throughput, cost and developer experience across mobile, backend and web repositories. Run it unattended where the risk allows.

•
Close the loop across the SDLC: Extend agentic workflows beyond code generation into spec quality checks, test generation, automated review, CI failure triage and repair, release verification, and post-deploy signals, so the system improves from what happens after merge.

•
Prototype fast, then harden: Get a new workflow running in days, prove it on real tickets with real squads, and turn what holds up into production infrastructure.

•
Run AI in production properly: Agents in production take more than an API call. Own the eval sets, LLM-as-a-judge grading, versioning, tracing and dashboards that tell us whether a workflow change made things better, including the hardest case: a change that passes CI and is still wrong. Track the numbers that matter (merge rate, rework, time-to-signal, cost per change, escaped defects) and make them visible to engineers and leadership.

•
Make autonomy safe: Design sandboxing, permissions, human checkpoints and guardrails proportional to risk, with privacy by design as the default. Health data, security and infrastructure changes get stronger controls; low-risk, easily verified work runs hands-off.

•
Lead AI-native engineering by example: Set the bar for AI-augmented engineering across the organization.

EDDA is only as good as its actuators, and we're hiring the person who owns them. You will be our servo wizard: the single owner of every motor, actuator, gearbox and solenoid in the product, from the first torque and inertia calculation through supplier selection, bench characterization, control-loop tuning, abuse testing and production release. You are as fluent in gearbox design - backlash, torsional stiffness, efficiency, lubrication, lifetime - as you are inside the current loop of the servo driving it. And you have lived with motion systems that get rained on, dropped, fired next to and bounced across a field on the back of a truck.

What You'll Own

Everything in the product that converts electrons into motion is yours - the parts, the suppliers, the test data and the tuning.

- Motors and actuators: BLDC/PMSM and frameless torque motors, steppers where they earn their place, linear actuators - every axis that moves EDDA's azimuth, elevation and auxiliary mechanisms.

- Gearboxes and drivetrain: planetary, strain-wave (harmonic), cycloidal, worm and belt stages; the direct-drive-versus-geared call on each axis; bearing arrangements, preload, backlash and the stiffness budget that sets achievable control bandwidth.

- Solenoids and discrete actuators: latches, safeties, indexing and release mechanisms - the fast, simple actuators that must work every time, in the cold, after being dropped.

- Motor drives and tuning: drive selection or specification, commutation and feedback (encoders, resolvers, Hall sensors), current/velocity/position loop tuning, feedforward and filtering.

- Characterization and test: dynamometer and bench rigs, thermal derating, torque ripple and cogging, efficiency maps, endurance and abuse testing, and the acceptance tests production runs on every unit.

- The actuation supply chain: vendor qualification, custom motor and gearbox specifications, second sources, cost-down and the lead times that production depends on.

Essential Duties

- Size and select: turn slew-rate, acceleration, pointing-accuracy and duty-cycle requirements into torque, speed, reflected-inertia and thermal budgets; pick or specify the motor, gear ratio and drive that meet them with margin - and show the math.

- Design the drivetrain: own the mechanical path from rotor to load - gear stages, couplings, shafts, bearings, preload, lubrication and seals - and the stiffness and backlash budget that determines how hard the loops can be pushed.

- Characterize everything: build the rigs and run the tests - torque constant, back-EMF, inductance, cogging and ripple, friction and stiction, efficiency, thermal rise, backlash and lost motion - so tuning starts from a measured plant, not a datasheet.

- Tune the loops: commission and tune current, velocity and position loops (PID, feedforward, notch filters, observers) for aggressive high-bandwidth tracking without exciting structural modes or cooking the motor.

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.
The Role
BJAK builds technology products used across Southeast Asia. Doit App Sdn. Bhd. is the group’s digital wallet business in Malaysia, preparing to apply to Bank Negara Malaysia for approval to issue electronic money.

The Head of Risk & Compliance owns risk and compliance for Doit App end to end, from the licence application through to running the control function once the approval is granted. The first year is the application itself, so this is a build role rather than a maintenance one.

The role covers compliance, risk management, AML/CFT/CPF as the designated Compliance Officer at management level, and data protection as Doit App’s data protection officer.

You will report to the Board of Doit App Sdn. Bhd., with administrative reporting lines to Doit App’s Chief Executive and to BJAK’s Head of Risk & Compliance.
What You'll Own

• Owning the risk and compliance content of the application to Bank Negara Malaysia, and the engagement with the Bank from pre-application through to approval.

• Building and running the compliance framework, which is the monitoring plan, the registers, and the breach and corrective action process.

• Building the risk management framework, the risk appetite statement and the risk register, and reporting material risks to the Board.

• Safeguarding of customer funds, including keeping the electronic money float separate from the company’s own money and operating the trust account.

• The anti-money laundering programme as a reporting institution, covering risk assessment, customer due diligence, screening, suspicious transaction reporting, record keeping and training.

• Oversight of the white label partner and other outsourcing arrangements, making sure what each party is responsible for is written down and evidenced rather than assumed.

• Owning conflicts of interest, anti-bribery and corruption, whistleblowing, complaints, and personal data protection.

• Owning regulatory reporting and notifications to the Bank within their deadlines, and the compliance and risk reporting that goes to the Board.

• Reviewing onboarding flows, product additions, disclosures and marketing before they ship, and running compliance training across the team.

What We're Looking For

• A degree or professional qualification from an institution recognised by the government of Malaysia.

• 5+ years of relevant experience in financial services, including 3 in a compliance, regulatory or risk role at an institution regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia.

• Experience across both risk management and compliance. This is a combined function and not a specialist seat.

• Command of the Financial Services Act 2013, BNM’s policy document on Electronic Money, and BNM’s AML/CFT/CPF requirements and AMLA 2001.

• Familiarity with BNM’s requirements on technology risk, outsourcing, electronic know your customer, complaints handling and fair treatment of financial consumers.

• Experience dealing directly with Bank Negara on submissions, supervisory queries and compliance reviews.

The scope of work may include:

• Preparing and circulating a monthly newsletter with updates on energy news, relevant legislation, and regulatory filings, particularly those relevant to the Railbelt utilities

• Engaging with partner organizers across the state to understand the needs of communities

• Promoting volunteer involvement in AETP to build our base of knowledgeable and engaged citizens

• Editing articles from other contributors

• Participating in collaborative fundraising efforts for the Alaska Energy Project

• Maintaining/updating the AETP website as needed

Duration
This contract is at will and begins on the date determined by the Editor and the Project. This contract will remain in effect for future notice, unless otherwise determined by either party.
Compensation
Contractor shall be entitled to compensation for performing Services related to the Scope of Work. Compensation is for 20 hours of work per week at $30/hour DOE until this agreement is terminated or modified.
About AETP
AETP Guiding Document
Statement of need:
In Alaska, there is limited publicly available and universally digestible information about energy issues in the State, including information needed for the public and electric utility cooperative members to make educated decisions. Often, news outlets will discuss energy issues through an economic or a highly technical framework, but it is rare that these issues are shared in a digestible format for a general audience. The lack of information inhibits public engagement, particularly among member-owners of electric cooperatives. As a result, issues involving the public interest receive limited public engagement. The founders of the Alaska Energy Transparency Project recognize a need for both accurate, digestible information and reporting, as well as a platform for community engagement in this area.
Mission:
Maintain a respected news outlet for energy democracy issues to promote community engagement around electric utilities and other energy issues. Engage member-owners in the process of democratizing energy issues through citizen journalism. Monitor the work of the four Railbelt cooperatives, placing it in its larger regulatory and legislative context when necessary.
Goals:

• Bring transparency and digestibility to the decisions being made at the Railbelt utilities and other regulatory entities

• Foster conversations about energy issues among the public, particularly among ratepayers

Output:

• Online platform for journalistic and community information.

• Monthly newsletter with links to other sources and brief capsules of co-op news.

Format:
Layout: Four main sections:

• Journalistic content: Investigative and news reporting written to journalistic standards (objective reporting, no word count cap)

• Community perspectives: Observations, eyewitness accounts, and opinions from community members about energy issues (cap at 3,000 words)

• Elections: Dedicated page for information about cooperative board elections

• Reference: Short pieces explaining important concepts, glossary of frequently used terms in energy discussions, list of acronyms

Funding:
No funding will be accepted from entities for reporting about those entities, funding will be grants-based and member-sourced, but there will be no paywall.
